title: Reading the icons on the screens
target: How to read the line icons a Supermarket Simulator screen uses, given that they are drawn in families and numbered per family rather than named by subject.
prerequisites: A shop open long enough to reach a screen
The tablet or the shop computer in front of you

steps.do: Treat the small marks on a screen as words rather than as decoration.
steps.because: the build names line icons in families of its own (icon_line_shopping_14, icon_line_tool_44, icon_line_weather_18)

steps.do: Learn the family before the individual mark.
steps.because: the icons are sorted into a shopping set, a tool set, a weather set, an arrow set, a gesture set, a game set and a common set (icon_line_arrow_1, icon_line_gesture_34, icon_line_game_40)

steps.do: Read the object the icon shows rather than the number in its name.
steps.because: some of them are a plain object: a trolley, a bin and a water drop (icon_line_shopping_14, icon_line_tool_44, icon_line_weather_18)

steps.do: Do not wait for a label to appear beside an icon.
steps.because: the icons are numbered per family rather than named by subject (icon_line_arrow_2, icon_line_arrow_15, icon_line_common_74)

steps.do: Watch for the app icons drawn in the same style.
steps.because: app icons are carried beside the line set (icon_app_78)

steps.do: Expect the same drawing to come back on another screen.
steps.because: the common family is reused across the game's own screens (icon_line_common_28, icon_line_common_77)

commonMistakes: Hunting for a word beside an icon that has none.
Treating two icons from different families as the same mark.
Guessing a number in an icon's name means something in the shop.
Learning one screen's icons and expecting them to mean something else elsewhere.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
